questions_and_answers.question: What are the nominative forms of the familiar pronouns in German?
Which cases are shown in the table of forms for dein and euer?
Which possessive words correspond to du and ihr?
What is the accusative form of euer for a masculine noun?
Which statement is correct regarding the forms of dein?

answers.answer: They correspond exactly to the forms of mein and sein

questions_and_answers.question: What shorter form does euer take before endings?

How would you say 'Where is yours?' when referring to a sweater?
Which example shows the use of euer in the dative plural?

answers.answer: Könnten wir in eurem Wagen mitfahren?

questions_and_answers.question: Which sentence illustrates the use of the familiar possessive adjective standing alone when the noun is understood?

answers.answer: Das ist mein Pullover. Wo ist deiner?

Wir werden um halb vier fahren
Die forms of dein correspond exactly to those of mein

articles.text:
B. PRONOUNS AND POSSESSIVE WORDS IN FAMILIAR SPEECH
I. The three forms of the pronouns used in familiar or intimate speech are as follows:
Nominative: du – ihr
Accusative: dich – euch
Dative: dir – euch
We have seen how they are used in some of the basic sentences; here are a few additional examples:
Wie geht es Ihnen, Herr Becker? – Wie geht es dir, Klaus? – Na, Klaus und Gerhard, wie geht es euch?
Beeilen Sie sich! – Beeil’ dich! – Beeilt euch!
Lassen Sie sich die Haare schneiden. – Lass dir die Haare schneiden. – Lasst euch die Haare schneiden.
Ich hole Sie dort um eins ab. – Ich hole dich dort um eins ab. – Ich hole euch dort um eins ab.
Darf ich mit Ihnen mitfahren? – Darf ich mit dir mitfahren? – Darf ich mit euch mitfahren?

II. The possessive words that go with du and ihr are dein and euer. Like the other possessive words (see Unit 4) they are ein‑type specifiers and have the following forms:
with der‑nouns: dein (nom.), deinen (acc.), deinem (dat.), deines (gen.) – euer (nom.), euren (acc.), eurem (dat.), eures (gen.)
with das‑nouns: dein, dein, deinem, deines – euer, euer, eurem, eures
with die‑nouns: deine, deine, deiner, deiner – eure, eure, eurer, eurer
with plural nouns: deine, deine, deinen, deiner – eure, eure, euren, eurer
Note that the forms of dein correspond exactly to the forms of mein, sein, etc., as given in Unit 4. Note also that euer has a shorter form eur‑ before endings.

III. The familiar possessive words may occur in any of the ein‑type specifier sequences and also, in the special forms noted in Unit 4, standing alone when the noun is understood:
Hast du dein Frühstücksbrot? (Do you have your lunch?)
Ich will deinen grauen Anzug reinigen lassen. (I want to have your gray suit cleaned.)
Kannst du auch meine Oberhemden mitnehmen, wenn du deine in die Wäscherei bringst? (Can you also take my shirts along when you take yours to the laundry?)
Das ist mein Pullover. Wo ist deiner? (That is my sweater. Where is yours?)
Könnten wir in eurem Wagen mitfahren? (Could we ride in your car?)
Wollt ihr eure Sommeranzüge auch reinigen lassen? (Do you also want to have your summer suits cleaned?)
Das ist aber ein schöner Wagen! Ist das euer? (That is a beautiful car! Is that yours?)
